correctness.rationale: F_k(y,z)=(z e^-y/(1+kz),y e^-z/(1+ky)) maps each coordinate strictly below the opposite input, so both even subsequences decrease to zero. Taylor expansion of F_k^2 gives x_next=x(1-2kx-2t+O((x+t)^2)) and t_next=t(1-2x-2kt+O((x+t)^2)), whence S=x+t=Theta(1/m) and sum S diverges while sum S² converges. Exact L_next=-L-[phi_k(y)-phi_k(z)], phi_k(u)=u-log(1+ku), and order-reversal give increment of |L| equal phi_k(max)-phi_k(min). For k>1 sign eventually negative and ratio ->1, giving n y,n z ->1/(k+1). For k=1 the ratio tends positive finite and diagonal iff equal starts, producing complementary alternating profiles. For k<1 off-diagonal ratio separates; the dominant two-step component ~1/(2km), minority has exponent m^-1/k and a strictly positive constant by summability of logarithmic remainder. Independent code verified the exact ratio identity and regimes up to n=150000: k=.6 dominant n*y=1.66411 vs 1/k=1.66667, k=1 n(y+z)=.999974, k=1.5 n(y+z)=.797897 vs 2/(k+1)=.8; full k>1 ratio convergence is slower than these samples, consistent with asymptotic proof.
